summary: Phantom postbacks from decommissioned staging keys attributed to production invoice
description: Issue summary: Customer Acadia HealthTech reports charges on their latest invoice for embedding requests originating from staging API keys that were decommissioned on 2026-02-24. Impact: Unexpected invoice line for ~120k embed units (~$2,640) attributed to production billing; customer revenue-impacting and contract-level concern. Environment: Production (us-east-1), customer on enterprise plan with dedicated tenancy. Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer provided decommissioned key ID and sample timestamps 2) Query billing events and postback logs for the key range 2026-02-24..2026-03-08 3) Observe invoice line referencing org id and usage from those timestamps. Observed logs: Postback consumer processed 3 replay batches on 2026-03-02 03:12Z with metadata showing environment tag: "prod"; aggregator reconciled events and emitted usage postbacks to billing with org mapping to Acadia; message offset origin: kafka-topic:postback-v1, retained offsets from migration. Additional notes: Key was removed from key-service on 2026-02-24 but remained cached in edge-aggregator for ~14 days due to TTL misconfiguration. This allowed replayed messages after a region failover to be attributed without a decommission check.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Migration + TTL misconfig caused decommissioned keys to remain discoverable by postback path leading to attribution of replayed events.
Confirmed: Edge-aggregator cache TTL erroneously set to 14d post-migration; key-service had decommissioned key record; postback consumer did not check key-service before emitting usage postbacks.
Impact quantification: ~120,344 embed units attributed between 2026-03-01 03:00Z and 2026-03-02 04:00Z. Unit price for redwood-embed-1 at customer's tier: $0.022/unit; estimated amount: $2,647.57.
Risk: If left unpatched, similar replay events during migrations or rebalances could lead to incorrect billing for other enterprise customers.

Mitigation considered: immediate purge of aggregator caches + add pre-emit key-status check + retroactive reprocessing of affected postbacks to produce adjusted billing events. Chosen path: purge + pre-emit check + provisional credit followed by reprocessing in a controlled window.
resolution: Provisional credit approved and issued (FIN-4267). Hotfix deployed to postback-service with key-status verification (PR 1243) and aggregator TTL corrected to 1h; queue offsets for affected batches were replayed into a reprocessing pipeline that emits corrected postbacks. Finance will post a final credit memo on the next billing cycle. Follow-up actions: retroactive audit of recent region migrations for cache TTL changes, add an automated test to validate decommissioned-key handling, update runbook 'Postback Replay Runbook' with remediation steps and checklist.
resolution_notes: Workaround/fix: 1) Purged decommissioned-key cache from edge-aggregators and forced a consumer rebalance. 2) Deployed pr/1243 to enforce key-status check at postback emit time. 3) Issued provisional credit to Acadia and queued reprocess of affected offsets. Postmortem and runbook update scheduled. Customer finance team was provided a credit memo draft for their records.
